antecedent_conditions: Physical environment E with complexity level C (operationalized as fractal dimension, edge density, color diversity, or information-theoretic entropy). Person P shifts from activity frame A₁ (focused work: report completion, data analysis) to activity frame A₂ (creative exploration: brainstorming, design ideation).
predicted_outcome:
- C_opt(A₂) > C_opt(A₁): The optimal complexity for positive affect and performance shifts upward under the exploratory frame.
- Performance under A₁ peaks at lower C than under A₂ (inverted-U peak shifts right).
- At complexity levels above C_opt(A₁) but below C_opt(A₂), A₁ performance degrades while A₂ performance improves.
moderating_variables:
- Domain expertise (experts tolerate higher complexity in both frames; main effect of expertise + interaction with frame)
- Working memory capacity (higher WMC → larger shift between frames, because WMC enables the wider attentional scope required by exploration)
- Current cognitive load (external load narrows the tolerance band for both frames, reducing the shift between them)
- Introversion/extraversion (extraverts show larger shift toward higher complexity under exploration)
expected_effect_sizes:
- Complexity preference shift between frames: d ≈ 0.4–0.7
- Performance crossover (same complexity, different frames): d ≈ 0.5–0.8
- Expertise moderation: interaction β ≈ 0.15–0.25
neural_signature: Higher frontal theta (4–8 Hz) at the moment of frame shift (working memory engagement for new goal). Shift in posterior alpha power topography (parietal alpha suppression broader under exploration, narrower under focus). Beta-frequency PFC–posterior coherence reconfigures within 200–500ms of instruction.
architectural_test_case: Open-plan office with adjustable environmental complexity (movable screens, variable lighting complexity, adjustable visual density). Within-subjects design: same participants complete focused work task and creative brainstorming task in same physical space at varying complexity levels. Dependent variables: task performance, self-reported affect, eye-tracking (fixation entropy as implicit complexity processing measure), EEG.
overlap_analysis: Overlaps significantly with Berlyne's Complexity Goldilocks (Template 2: PP_COMPLEXITY_GOLDILOCKS_002). Ensure distinction is clear (IE sets the activity frame that *shifts* the Berlyne optimum).
name: Activity-Frame Complexity Retuning
